questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about speculative demand for money?

i. It is Perfectly interest elastic

ii. It is Relatively interest elastic

iii. It is Perfectly interest inelastic

iv. It is Relatively interest inelastic
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Only ii.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• It is Perfectly interest elastic:

 
 
• This statement is incorrect.
 
• Speculative demand for money is not perfectly interest elastic because it depends on expectations about future interest rate movements.
 
• It is influenced by various factors such as expectations about future interest rates, risk perceptions, and alternative investment opportunities.
 
 
 
• It is Relatively interest elastic:
 
 
• This statement is correct.
 
• Speculative demand for money is relatively interest elastic because it responds to changes in interest rates, albeit not proportionately.
 
• When interest rates are expected to rise, people may prefer to hold less money and invest in interest-bearing assets instead.
 
• Conversely, when interest rates are expected to fall, people may prefer to hold more money.
 
 
 
• It is Perfectly interest inelastic:
 
 
• This statement is incorrect.
 
• Speculative demand for money is not perfectly interest-inelastic because it does respond to changes in interest rates, although not as strongly as some other forms of demand for money.
 
 
 
• It is Relatively interest inelastic:
 
 
• This statement is incorrect.
 
• As mentioned earlier, speculative demand for money is relatively interest elastic, not relatively interest inelastic
 
 
 
• 
 
hence only ii __is correct.

questions.question: Which of the following is enforceable by the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fundamental rights**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental rights** are enforceable by the **Indian Constitution **as they provide citizens with certain rights and freedoms that the government must protect.
 
• Fundamental rights include the right to equality, freedom of speech and expression, and the right to life and personal liberty.
 
• The **Preamble** is not enforceable in a court of law, but it does provide the **basic structure and values **of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Directive principles** of state policy are **guidelines** for the government to follow, but they are not enforceable in a court of law.
 
• **Fundamental duties **are **obligations** that citizens are expected to fulfill, but they are not enforceable in a court of law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Indian Constitution** is the **supreme law** of the land and provides the framework for the government and its citizens.
 
• On **November 26, 1949**, the Constituent Assembly enacted the Indian Constitution, which became operative on **January 26, 1950.**
 
• **Directive principles** of state policy include provisions for a **just and equitable society**,** protection of the environment**, and **promotion of education** and **healthcare**.
 
• **Fundamental duties** include respecting the **Constitution and national flag**, promoting harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood, and protecting public property.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a flow concept?

options.text: Number of machines used in a factory

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Number of machines used in a factory.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Flow concept** refers to a** variable **that is measured over a period of time, such as** revenue, expenses, production, or consumption**.
 
• **Profit of a corporation** and **output produced** by a firm are flow concepts because they are measured over a **specific period**, such as **a year, a quarter,** or a month.
 
• **Interest expense** on a loan is also a flow concept because it represents the **amount of money** paid or accrued over time to borrow money.
 
• **Number of machines** used in a factory is** NOT** a flow concept because it is a **stock concept** that represents the quantity of a resource at a specific point in time, rather than the rate of change or flow of that resource.
 
• Other examples of stock concepts include **inventory, capital, assets, liabilities, and equity.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Any quantity that can be measured **over time** is referred to as **flow**, whereas **stock** refers to any quantity that can only be measured at a **specific moment** in time.
 
• The flow and the stock are** mutually dependent**.
 
• Stock affects flow because **more capital** will result in a** higher flow** of services.
 
• Flow affects stock; for example, an economy's** increased money supply** leads to an** increase** in the total amount of **money**.

questions.question: Import substitution strategy is commonly called _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"**__**Inward looking trade strategy.**__**"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Import substitution strategy** refers to a government policy aimed at promoting **domestic production** by substituting imported goods with domestically produced goods.
 
• Import substitution strategy is also known as **inward looking trade strategy **which aims to produce goods domestically which are imported to our nation.
 
• This strategy involves **imposing tariffs** and other trade barriers on** imported goods** to make them more expensive and less competitive in the domestic market.
 
• The** goal** of import substitution is to **reduce a country's reliance on imports **and build up its domestic industries, which can lead to economic growth and development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**Make in India campaign**," is a government initiative to promote **manufacturing and investment** in India.

 
 
• The **Prime Minister** introduced the Made in India program in **September 2014 **as a component of a larger series of nation-building programs.
 
 
 
• "**Outward looking trade strategy**," refers to a policy of** promoting exports** and opening up to international trade.
 
 
• The widely recognized definition of the **outward-oriented trade strategy** based on price incentives is when the** effective exchange rate** (EERx) of the nation is lower than its **import rate** (EERm).
 
 
 
• "**Balanced trade strategy**," refers to a policy of maintaining a **balance between imports and exports**.
 
 
• **Controlling inflation **and **enforcing tariffs** or other barriers, including **import certificates**, on a country-by-country basis are two ways to implement balanced trade.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is true?

A) Higher inflation means lower real GDP, ceteris paribus

B) Price Index is 200 if nominal GDP and real GDP are the same
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only A.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A** higher inflation rate** indicates that the **general price level **of goods and services in an economy is **increasing**.
 
• This means that consumers will have to** pay more **for the same goods and services, resulting in a decrease in their purchasing power.
 
• As a result, businesses will produce less, leading to **lower real GDP.**
 
• This **relationship **between** inflation and real GDP** is known as the **Phillips Curve**, which suggests an inverse relationship between the two variables.
 
• However, it is important to note that this relationship holds only in the **short run**.
 
• In the **long run**, the **Phillips Curve** becomes **vertical**, indicating that there is **no tradeoff **between inflation and real GDP.
 
• **Higher inflation** does lead to **lower real GDP** in the short run, ceteris paribus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A country's **market value** of all the **finished goods and services **significant to a particular economic sector, are used to measure** inflation**.
 
• **Price indices**, which focus on the **costs of a variety of goods and services** significant to a particular economic sector, are used to measure inflation.
 
• A positive relationship between inflation and real GDP, is not supported by economic theory or empirical evidence.
 
• **Nominal GDP** and **real GDP** are not always equal.
 
• **Nominal GDP** is the total value of goods and services produced in an economy, measured at current prices, while **real GDP** adjusts for inflation and measures economic output in constant dollars.

questions.question: Who introduced Mansabdari system into the administration under the Mughals?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mansabdari system **was introduced by **Akbar** during his reign in the Mughal Empire.
 
• The system was a **hierarchical ranking system** based on **military and administrative roles**.
 
• It was designed to ensure **loyalty and control** over the nobility and military officials.
 
• The system required officials to maintain a certain number of** soldiers and horses**, and their rank was determined by the number of soldiers and horses they maintained.
 
• Akbar also introduced the concept of **dual government**, where the empire was divided into provinces and each province was governed by a governor and a revenue collector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **​**From **1628 until 1658**, he was king.
 
 
 
• **Aurangzeb** was the **sixth** Mughal Emperor and is known for his religious policies and expansion of the empire.
 
 
• ​From **1658** until his passing in **1707,** he was king.
 
 
 
• **Jahangir** was the **fourth** Mughal Emperor and is known for his love for art and culture.

questions.question: Which of the following indicators is the best to assess the living standard of people?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Physical quality of life index.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Physical Quality of Life Index** (PQLI) is the best indicator to assess the living standard of people as it takes into account** three **basic dimensions of human life: **basic literacy, life expectancy, and infant mortality rate.**
 
• PQLI is a **comprehensive indicator** that measures the **overall well-being of people**, including their health, education, and standard of living.
 
• **Literacy rate** is an important indicator of the** educational level** of people, but it does not provide a complete picture of their living standard.
 
• **Neonatal mortality rate** and **maternal mortality** rate are important health indicators, but they **do not capture the full range** of factors that affect the living standard of people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Literacy rate:**

 
 
• It is the percentage of people who can** read and write** in a given population.
 
• It is an important indicator of the **educational level of people** and their ability to access information and participate in the economy and society.
 
 
 
• **Neonatal mortality rate:**
 
 
• It is the **number of deaths of infants** under 28 days of age per 1,000 live births in a given population.
 
• It is an important** health indicator** that reflects the quality of **maternal and child health care** and the overall level of development of a society.
 
 
 
• **Maternal mortality rate:**
 
 
• It is the number of deaths of women due to **pregnancy or childbirth-related complications** per 100,000 live births in a given population.
 
• According to UN inter-agency projections, the **worldwide maternal mortality ratio **(MMR) decreased by **34% **between 2000 and 2020, from 339 deaths to 223 deaths per 100,000 live births.

questions.question: Lactitol is derived through the hydrogenation of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lactose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Lactitol is a** sugar alcohol** that is commonly used as a **low-calorie sweetener** and a **bulking agent** in various food products.
 
• It is derived through the **hydrogenation of lactose**, which is a disaccharide composed of glucose and galactose.
 
• **Glucose** is a **monosaccharide** that is commonly used as a sweetener and a source of energy in the body, but it is not directly involved in the production of lactitol.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lactose** is a** natural sugar** found in **milk and dairy products**, and it is commonly used as a substrate for the production of lactitol through hydrogenation.
 
• **Maltose** is a** natural sugar** found in** grains and malt products**, and it is commonly used as a substrate for the production of other sugar alcohols such as maltitol and sorbitol.
 
 
• Maltose is a disaccharide composed of two glucose molecules
 
 
 
• **Lactic acid** is commonly used as a **food preservative and a flavoring agent**, and it is also produced in the body during intense exercise and certain medical conditions.
 
 
• Lactic acid is a byproduct of anaerobic metabolism in muscle cells and certain bacteria
 
 
 
• **Glucose** is a primary source of energy for the body and is commonly used as a** sweetener and a bulking agent** in various food products.
 
 
• It can also be produced through the **hydrolysis of starch and other carbohydrates**.

• The **sodium test** is a test used to detect the presence of **sodium ions **in a sample.
 
 
• It involves the use of a reagent such as , which reacts with sodium ions to form a yellow precipitate.

• Fiat money is a currency that has value because the government has declared it to be **legal tender**.

• **Rs. 500 currency note** is an example of fiat money as it is a currency note issued by the RBI and has value because the government has declared it to be legal tender.
 
• Rather than the value of the commodity supporting it, the value of fiat money is determined by the **relationship of supply and demand **as well as the **stability of the issuing government**.

• Instead, the **government** is the one issuing the money.
 
• Rs. **200 bank cheque** is not an example of fiat money as it is not a currency issued by the RBI.
 
 
• It is a **negotiable instrument** that represents the funds in a bank account.
 
 
 
• Rs.** 20 coin** is an example of fiat money as it is a coin** issued by the RBI** and has value because the government has declared it to be** legal tender**.
 
• Rs.** 10 coin** is also an example of fiat money as it is a coin issued by the RBI and has value because the government has declared it to be **legal tender**.
